result.summary:
Read test/specs/REQ-083.md and test/letflow/routers/tasks_test.exs in full (not TEST-DESIGNER's handoff summary as a substitute), plus step-00's requirement text and step-03's own claims for cross-reference only. Independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/tasks_test.exs` myself: real output ends `Finished in 18.4 seconds (0.00s async, 18.4s sync)` / `Result: 23 passed` -- 0 failed, matching TEST-DESIGNER's claim with my own measured run, not a copied claim.

Per-check results:

(a) Every AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC7 has at least one runnable test; AC6 is correctly a documented no-test-needed (pure moduledoc criterion, REVIEWER already confirmed the text against the shipped file per step-02d finding 6 -- re-checked lib/letflow/tasks.ex's moduledoc lines 11-40 myself, contains the ported/not-ported table). No `@tag :skip` anywhere in the file (grepped, zero matches) -- PASS.

(b) Grepped test/specs/REQ-083.md for 'TODO'/'implement test' -- zero matches. Every AC section states a concrete 'why this test exists' rationale distinct from restating the criterion (verified by reading each section, not just checking non-emptiness) -- PASS.

(c) Every describe block either has its own `setup do: %{tenant: TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!(slug_prefix: "req083-<unique>")}` or inlines a fresh `provisioned_tenant!/1` call with a distinct slug_prefix per test (grepped all occurrences: req083-getbyid, req083-list-page, req083-inbox-page, req083-inbox-scope, req083-role-iso-a/-b, req083-cross-a/-b, req083-iso-a/-b, req083-allowlist, req083-403, req083-route-order, req083-validation, req083-status-filter, req083-assignee-id, req083-inv2, req083-notfound, req083-unmatched -- all distinct strings, each provisioning a real distinct tenant schema). All task/user/group/role ids are `Ecto.UUID.generate/0` or DB-assigned on insert -- no shared hardcoded UUID or username literal reused across tests -- PASS.

(d) `async: false` module-wide but each test provisions its own tenant fixture from scratch inside its own setup/body and asserts only on state it itself created; no test reads state left by a sibling test, no shared module-level mutable fixture. Self-sufficient -- PASS.

(e) Grepped for password/secret/token/connection-string patterns: only hit is `password_hash: "__NO_PASSWORD_SET__"`, an obvious placeholder sentinel, not a real credential; no connection strings, API keys, or real secrets anywhere in the file -- PASS.

Security-sensitive scrutiny (per ORCH's specific dispatch, given this run's INV-1 rework cycle):

1. AC2 inbox test (lines 253-289 of tasks_test.exs): confirmed the four assertions are four genuinely separate `assert`/`refute` lines (`assert task_direct.id in returned_ids`, `assert task_via_group.id in returned_ids`, `assert task_via_role.id in returned_ids`, `refute task_other_user.id in returned_ids`) -- not collapsed into a single set-equality or `Enum.all?` check. Each targets a distinct assignee_type arm (USER-direct, GROUP, ROLE, USER-other). Genuinely 4 separate checks -- PASS.

2. Cross-tenant role-leak test (lines 292-325, 'AC2 extra assurance'): read lib/letflow/tasks.ex's `resolve_principal_scope/2` (lines 219-235) directly -- it issues `from(t in TenantRole, ...)` with `prefix: prefix` passed through to `Repo.all/Repo.one`, a real `:prefix`-scoped Ecto query against the tenant schema, not a mock or stub. The test itself provisions two REAL distinct tenant schemas (tenant_a, tenant_b via `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1`), inserts a real TenantRole row named "approver" bound to a real group in tenant_b via `insert_role!/3` (which itself writes directly to the prefix-scoped TenantRole table, matching the design's rework-1 fix), and asserts the tenant-A caller's inbox contains their own task and never the tenant-B role task. This exercises the real reworked query path against real per-tenant fixture data, not a stubbed prefix -- PASS.

3. AC3/INV-5 cross-tenant-vs-nonexistent test (lines 331-350): confirmed it asserts BOTH `resp_cross_tenant.status == resp_never_existed.status` AND `resp_cross_tenant.resp_body == resp_never_existed.resp_body` -- byte-identical body comparison, not merely status-code parity -- PASS.

4. AC5/INV-2 field-allowlist test (lines 381-415): confirmed both assertions use `Map.keys(item) |> Enum.sort() == @task_list_item_keys` / `Map.keys(body) |> Enum.sort() == @task_detail_keys` -- full sorted key-set equality, not `Map.has_key?/2` presence checks on a subset -- plus six explicit individual `refute Map.has_key?/2` calls for the named exclusions (claimed_by, form_schema, output_variables, completed_by, completed_at, cancelled_at). Note: @task_detail_keys is itself built via `Enum.sort(@task_list_item_keys ++ [...])` at compile time (a fixed literal list, not derived from runtime data), so the sort call there is normalizing a hardcoded expected list, not laundering the actual/expected comparison -- the actual side (`Map.keys(body) |> Enum.sort()`) is still a real runtime sort of the live response. Correct and matches the documented fix for TEST-DESIGNER's own found bug (unsorted comparison) -- PASS.

Also independently spot-verified two implementation claims underpinning the test design rather than trusting them: (i) `Letflow.Routers.Tasks.handle_list_result/2` maps `{:error, :invalid_cursor}` to `Response.unprocessable/2` (422), confirmed at lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex lines 254-259 -- matches the spec's stated deliberate divergence from identity_test.exs's 400-for-cursor precedent; (ii) other validation paths (status/instance_id/malformed id) do use `Response.bad_request/2` (400), confirmed at lines 169/172/290 -- matches the spec's stated R-Co-422-vs-this-router-400 divergence note.

No check failed. No partial-credit override applied.
